name: Visa-free entry as a tourist
summary: Many nationalities enter Uruguay without a visa, including most of the Americas, the EU, the US, Canada, Japan, Australia and New Zealand. The official list is by country. Work or stays beyond 90 days need prior consultation.

other: Check your passport on the official visa regime table.
Stay length for each nationality was not confirmed on the page, so check the table before you travel.

sources.label: Ministerio del Interior: Régimen de visas de admisión

name: Consular entry visa (tourism, business, study, work, family, humanitarian)
summary: Nationalities not on the visa-exempt list need a visa from a Uruguayan consulate before arriving. Categories include tourism, business, work, study, family reunification, humanitarian and congress visas.

other: Needs an invitation letter or a confirmed hotel booking, plus proof of financial means.
Passport must be valid at least 6 months after arrival.
Business visitors need an invitation letter from the company.
Consular fees change every January 1.

steps: Contact the Uruguayan consulate that covers where you live.
Attend your appointment in person with your documents.
The Consul interviews you and sends the file to the national migration office (DNM).
The consulate tells you the result. If approved, the visa is stamped in your passport and you have 60 days to enter.

fees.label: Visa fee, charged only if granted

processing: DNM approval usually takes at least 20 business days, per the official page.

sources.label: gub.uy: Inicio de solicitud de visas
MRREE: Visas para ingresar a Uruguay
Ministerio del Interior: Régimen de visas de admisión

name: Digital nomad provisional identity sheet (Hoja de identidad provisoria)
summary: A short permit for people who work for themselves or for companies abroad. You enter as a tourist, apply online, and get 6 months, extendable by 6 more for a total of one year.

other: Enter Uruguay as a regular tourist.
Signed sworn statement that you can support yourself. No minimum income is set.
For the extension: criminal record certificate from every country where you lived 6+ months in the last 5 years, plus a Uruguayan vaccination certificate.

steps: Enter Uruguay as a tourist.
Apply online with a gub.uy account, attaching the signed sworn statement.
Apply for the 6 month extension with the criminal record and vaccination documents.
After approval, finish issuance at the civil identification office (DNIC).
documents: Copy of the ID or passport used to enter

fees.label: Procedure fee (55.71 UI), cannot be paid from abroad

sources.label: Agesic: Permiso especial de residencia legal
Ministerio del Interior: Types of residencies in Uruguay

name: Temporary residence (work, business, religious)
summary: Residence for foreigners with a job or activity in Uruguay. Workers need a letter from the employer with role, contract length and monthly pay. Granted for 6 months to 2 years and renewable.

other: Pay must be at least the national minimum wage, or stated maintenance.
Criminal record certificate, vaccination certificate and occupational health card (Carné de Salud Laboral) required.
If your nationality needs a visa, it must be valid.

stay.note: Minimum 6 months, maximum 2 years per grant, extendable. Request renewal within 90 days before it expires.

steps: Start online with a gub.uy account or book an appointment.
Upload the documents as PDFs and pay.
DNM reviews, then you book an appointment.
Attend with the original documents.
documents: Employer letter plus notarized company certificate or BPS work history

fees.label: Residence permit (557.30 UI, indexed units)
Migration certificate for ID card (55.70 UI)
Re-entry permit, each exit while pending (225.60 UI)

name: Temporary residence (student)
summary: Residence for students at Uruguayan schools. Granted for up to 1 year at a time and renewable, up to 2 years total for the course.

other: Official certificate from the institution (notarized if private).
Proof of enough money to live on, from a relative or from abroad (notarized statement).

stay.note: Up to 1 year, renewable in equal periods, max 2 years total for the course.

fees.label: Residence permit (557.30 UI, indexed units)
Migration certificate for ID card (55.70 UI)
Re-entry permit, each exit while pending (225.60 UI)

sources.label: Ministerio del Interior: Types of residencies in Uruguay

name: Temporary residence (family of a temporary resident)
summary: Spouses, minor children and parents of people holding certain temporary residences can get temporary residence for the same period as the holder.

other: Proof of the family tie is required.
Based on the 2019 foreign ministry page. Confirm current rules with DNM.

name: Temporary residence for Mercosur and associated states nationals
summary: Nationals of Mercosur members and associated states can live in Uruguay on a 2 year temporary residence. No job offer needed. It can be renewed once and then converted to permanent.

other: Passport, birth certificate, criminal record from the last 5 years of residence, vaccination certificate and occupational health card.
Also open to people naturalized in these countries 5+ years, per the Interior page.

stay.note: Renewable once for another 2 years. Request within 90 days before expiry.

fees.label: Residence permit (557.30 UI, indexed units)
Migration certificate for ID card (55.70 UI)
Re-entry permit, each exit while pending (225.60 UI)

name: Permanent residence for Mercosur and associated states nationals
summary: Permanent residence for nationals of Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Bolivia, Paraguay, Peru, Ecuador, Colombia, Venezuela, Suriname and Guyana. Paraguay and Brazil are exempt from the fee.

other: Valid ID, 5 year criminal record, Uruguayan vaccination certificate.

fees.label: Residence permit (557.30 UI, indexed units)
Migration certificate for ID card (55.70 UI)
Re-entry permit, each exit while pending (225.60 UI)

steps: Start online with a gub.uy account.
Upload documents and pay.
DNM reviews, then book an appointment.
Attend with originals.

sources.label: Ministerio del Interior: Types of residencies in Uruguay

name: Permanent residence (any nationality)
summary: Open to any foreigner who wants to live in Uruguay for good. You show monthly income enough to live on. The official page sets no minimum amount or minimum years.

other: Proof of livelihood: employee, self-employed or business owner, or foreign or local pensioner.
Criminal record, vaccination certificate and health card.
No set income figure on the official page.

fees.label: Residence permit (557.30 UI, indexed units)
Migration certificate for ID card (55.70 UI)
Re-entry permit, each exit while pending (225.60 UI)

steps: Start online and select Permanente.
Upload documents and pay.
DNM reviews, then book an appointment.
Attend with originals.

name: Permanent residence through a Uruguayan family tie
summary: Children, spouses, registered partners and siblings of Uruguayans can apply for permanent residence directly. No temporary residence first. Parents may also qualify, but the sources disagree.

other: Proof of the relationship, issued within 1 year if foreign.
The gub.uy page lists child, spouse, partner and sibling. Older foreign ministry and Interior pages also list parents. Confirm with DNM.

fees.label: Residence permit (557.30 UI, indexed units)
Migration certificate for ID card (55.70 UI)

name: Retiree and pensioner residence (Law 16.340)
summary: Foreigners with a foreign pension can apply through a Uruguayan consulate. Needs a pension above USD 1,500 a month and either a USD 100,000 home or USD 100,000 in government bonds. Based on a 2019 page, so confirm it is still in force.

investment.note: Home in Uruguay or government bonds held at BROU for 10 years

other: Source is a 2019 foreign ministry page. Check current rules.

name: Humanitarian visa and asylum
summary: Uruguay lists a humanitarian and emergency visa for documented cases. This record only points to the official visa page. Asylum procedure details were not confirmed.

other: Justified, documented grounds or cases authorized by the competent authority.
Asylum process not checked. Ask a Uruguayan consulate or the refugee authority.

sources.label: MRREE: Visas para ingresar a Uruguay

name: Legal citizenship (ciudadanía legal)
summary: Foreigners can get the carta de ciudadanía after 3 years of habitual residence with family in Uruguay, or 5 years without family. You also need good conduct, a livelihood and Spanish. It is free.

eligibility.language: Understand and speak Spanish if it is not your first language
other: Good conduct, plus capital in a business or property, or a science, art or trade.
Proof of livelihood for the full 3 or 5 years.
Two witnesses over 25 who have known you 3 or 5 years and are not relatives or employers.
Trips abroad over 6 consecutive months restart the count.
Citizenship rights cannot be used until 3 years after the certificate is granted (Constitution art. 75).

citizenship.note: 3 years with family in Uruguay, 5 years without. Dual citizenship not addressed on the official page.

steps: Get a residence and migration movements certificate from DNM.
Book a slot online (Montevideo, released on Mondays around 10:00).
Attend at Ituzaingó 1467 with documents and witnesses.
The Corte Electoral requests your criminal record itself.

fees.label: Free procedure

name: Natural citizenship by descent
summary: Children of a Uruguayan father or mother are natural citizens wherever they were born. If born abroad, you must settle in Uruguay and register in the Registro Cívico.

other: One Uruguayan parent.
Settle in Uruguay and register in the civic registry.

citizenship.note: One parent, first generation. Generations beyond that were not confirmed.

name: Natural citizenship by birth in Uruguay
summary: Anyone born in Uruguayan territory is a natural citizen.
